CLINICAL HISTORY
Diagnosis: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC)
Specimen Type: Tissue blocks

TEST PERFORMED
Fluorescence In Situ Hybridization (FISH) Analysis

METHODOLOGY
Interphase FISH analysis was performed on formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissue sections. Analysis was correlated with H&E stained slides to ensure adequate tumor representation.

Probes Used:
- Vysis ALK Break Apart FISH Probe Kit (Abbott Molecular)
- CytoVue SPEC ROS1 Dual Color Break Apart Probe (Empire Genomics)

Analysis: 50 interphase nuclei were scored for each probe set from two separate tissue blocks.

RESULTS

ALK (2p23) Gene Rearrangement Analysis:
Result: NEGATIVE
No evidence of ALK rearrangement detected
Cells analyzed: 50 cells from each of 2 tissue blocks (100 cells total)
Interpretation criteria: <15% of cells with split signals

ROS1 (6q22) Gene Rearrangement Analysis:
Result: NEGATIVE
No evidence of ROS1 rearrangement detected
Cells analyzed: 50 cells from each of 2 tissue blocks (100 cells total)
Interpretation criteria: <15% of cells with split signals

OVERALL CLASSIFICATION: ALK NEGATIVE

INTERPRETATION
FISH analysis demonstrates no evidence of ALK (2p23) or ROS1 (6q22) gene rearrangements in the tumor cells examined. The patient is classified as ALK negative per current testing guidelines.

CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE
ALK and ROS1 rearrangements are targetable molecular alterations found in approximately 5% and 1-2% of NSCLC cases, respectively. The absence of these rearrangements indicates that the patient would not benefit from ALK or ROS1 targeted tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy. Alternative treatment options should be considered based on other molecular findings and clinical factors.
